claim: India's benchmark 10-year G-Sec yield was 7.3707% on 12-Oct-2026, a three-year high after an eight-week rise of about 54 bp following RBI liquidity tightening and a repo-rate increase; an April-2026 report put it near 6.9%

author: bear-case
claim: Industry prepaid tariff rounds since the post-Jio price war: late Nov/Dec-2019; 26-Nov-2021 (Airtel +20-25%); 3-Jul-2024 (Airtel +10-21% after Jio's 27-Jun-2024 move); gaps of about 23 and 32 months; about 27 months have elapsed since the last round at the cutoff
source_title: India's Airtel hikes prepaid tariffs by 25%; Bharti Airtel raises mobile tariffs by up to 21%

author: bear-case
claim: Treating the three post-2019 rounds as a Poisson process (about 0.43 a year) gives P(at least one round in 5 years) of about 89% and P(at least two) of about 64%; counting only the two rounds after 2019 gives 76% and 42%
formula_or_inputs: lambda = 3 rounds / 6.9 years x 5; P(>=2) = 1 - e^-lambda (1 + lambda); input BEAR-C082
notes: Three events is a tiny sample; regime (three-plus-one players, Jio IPO) may differ

author: bear-case
claim: The draft base DCF (growth 12% fading to 7%, EBIT margin 33.5% to 37%, S/C 1.5) appears to carry no explicit industry tariff round: its year-1 growth matches organic drivers, the bull case is defined as 'two further tariff rounds', and the draft Layer 3 value adds a tariff round on top of the base
source_title: Draft valuation inputs and CIO scorecard
notes: If the base already embeds partial repair, variants V2-V5 overstate the uplift

author: bear-case
claim: Re-running the draft base DCF with the deterministic tool: draft base INR 1,215; with one realised +8% India mobile round in year 2 (90% EBIT flow-through) INR 1,378; with two rounds (years 2 and 5) INR 1,519
formula_or_inputs: Draft inputs (calc/valuation_dcf_inputs.json) with revenue growth +4.3pp in the round year (8% x mobile share 53.6% from BEAR-C098) and margin m'=(m+0.9u)/(1+u) thereafter
notes: Realised +8% is below the +14-16% realised ARPU the draft cites per past round

author: bear-case
claim: Normalising the risk-free rate from the 7.39% three-year high to 6.90% lowers Ke from 11.68% to 11.19% and WACC from 11.03% to 10.60%, lifting the draft base value from INR 1,215 to INR 1,341
formula_or_inputs: Ke = 6.90% - 1.87% + 0.87 x 7.08%; WACC = Ke x 0.8858 + 5.99% x 0.1142; inputs BEAR-C080, calc/valuation_wacc_inputs.json

author: bear-case
claim: Combining two tariff rounds with a normalised risk-free rate gives a base value of INR 1,672 (MoS -6%) and a re-mapped IA of about 44.7; adding a 25.17% tax rate gives INR 1,730 and IA about 46.0, holding every other draft IA score and the draft bear/bull values fixed
formula_or_inputs: IA1/IA2/IA4 re-mapped with SCORING.md anchors; E[IRR] built as the draft does (value x (1+Ke)^5 - FV of dividends); IA3 58, IA5 30, IA6 58, IA7 80, IA8 72 held; inputs BEAR-C085, BEAR-C086, BEAR-C099
notes: Steelman stack, not a recommended input set

claim: Re-weighting the draft's own scenarios toward the bull (15/50/35 or 10/45/45) moves E[IRR] to only 6.0-7.4% and IA to 36-37: scenario probabilities are not the swing factor; the base DCF value is

author: bear-case
claim: At INR 1,778.70, EV including minorities at market value (draft inputs) is about INR 13.76 lakh crore, 10.9x approximate TTM EBITDA; an owner holding the multiple constant earns about 10.4-11.6% a year over 5 years at 8% EBITDA growth, 12.6-13.7% at 10% and 14.8-15.9% at 12%; at the DCF-implied 8.2x exit the same paths give 3.3-8.9%
